originalComment: Calculates TO.
codeComment: This method calculates the end index (`to`) for a range based on the start index (`from`), the count of elements, and the total size of the collection. If the count is not -1, it adds the count to the start index and ensures the result does not exceed the total size.
codeFunctions: protected int calculateTo (final int from,final int count,final int size) { int to = size;if (count != - 1) { to = from + count;if (to > size) { to = size;} } return to;}

originalComment: Iterates collection.
codeComment: This method iterates over a collection, starting from a specified index, and invokes a JSP body for each item within the specified range. It uses an iterator to traverse the collection and sets attributes in the page context based on the current item's index.
codeFunctions: protected void iterateCollection (final Collection collection,final int from,final int count,final PageContext pageContext) throws JspException { JspFragment body = getJspBody ();Iterator iter = collection.iterator ();int i = 0;int to = calculateTo (from,count,collection.size ());while (i < to) { Object item = iter.next ();if (i >= from) { if (status != null) { iteratorStatus.next (!iter.hasNext ());} TagUtil.setScopeAttribute (var,item,scope,pageContext);TagUtil.invokeBody (body);} i ++;} }

originalComment: Iterates arrays.
codeComment: This method iterates over a portion of an array, setting attributes and invoking a JSP body for each item. It takes an array, a starting index, a count, and a PageContext as parameters. It calculates the end index, iterates over the specified range, sets attributes using TagUtil, and invokes the JSP body for each item.
codeFunctions: protected void iterateArray (final Object [ ] array,final int from,final int count,final PageContext pageContext) throws JspException { JspFragment body = getJspBody ();int len = array.length;int to = calculateTo (from,count,len);int last = to - 1;for (int i = from;i < to;i ++) { Object item = array [ i ];if (status != null) { iteratorStatus.next (i == last);} TagUtil.setScopeAttribute (var,item,scope,pageContext);TagUtil.invokeBody (body);} }

originalComment: Replaces all occurrences of a certain pattern in a string with a replacement string.This is the fastest replace function known to author.
codeComment: This method replaces all occurrences of a substring `sub` with another string `with` in the given string `s`. It handles the case where `sub` is an empty string by returning the original string `s`. The method uses a `StringBuilder` to efficiently build the resulting string by appending the original string before and after each occurrence of `sub`.
codeFunctions: public static String replace (final String s,final String sub,final String with) { if (sub.isEmpty ()) { return s;} int c = 0;int i = s.indexOf (sub,c);if (i == - 1) { return s;} int length = s.length ();StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (length + with.length ());do { sb.append (s,c,i);sb.append (with);c = i + sub.length ();} while ((i = s.indexOf (sub,c)) != - 1);if (c < length) { sb.append (s,c,length);} return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Replaces all occurrences of a character in a string.
codeComment: This method replaces all occurrences of a specified character (`sub`) in a given string (`s`) with another character (`with`). It first finds the index of the first occurrence of `sub` in `s`. If `sub` is not found, it returns the original string. Otherwise, it converts the string to a character array, replaces all occurrences of `sub` with `with`, and returns the modified string as a new string.
codeFunctions: public static String replaceChar (final String s,final char sub,final char with) { int startIndex = s.indexOf (sub);if (startIndex == - 1) { return s;} char [ ] str = s.toCharArray ();for (int i = startIndex;i < str.length;i ++) { if (str [ i ] == sub) { str [ i ] = with;} } return new String (str);}

originalComment: Replaces all occurrences of a characters in a string.
codeComment: This method takes a string `s` and two character arrays `sub` and `with`. It replaces each occurrence of any character in `sub` with the corresponding character in `with`. The method returns the modified string.
codeFunctions: public static String replaceChars (final String s,final char [ ] sub,final char [ ] with) { char [ ] str = s.toCharArray ();for (int i = 0;i < str.length;i ++) { char c = str [ i ];for (int j = 0;j < sub.length;j ++) { if (c == sub [ j ]) { str [ i ] = with [ j ];break;} } } return new String (str);}

originalComment: Replaces the very first occurrence of a substring with supplied string.
codeComment: This method replaces the first occurrence of a substring `sub` in a string `s` with another string `with`. If `sub` is not found in `s`, it returns `s` unchanged.
codeFunctions: public static String replaceFirst (final String s,final String sub,final String with) { int i = s.indexOf (sub);if (i == - 1) { return s;} return s.substring (0,i) + with + s.substring (i + sub.length ());}

originalComment: Replaces the very first occurrence of a character in a string.
codeComment: This method replaces the first occurrence of a specified character in a string with another character. It first finds the index of the specified character using the `indexOf` method. If the character is not found, it returns the original string. Otherwise, it creates a character array from the string, replaces the character at the found index with the new character, and returns the modified string as a new `String` object.
codeFunctions: public static String replaceFirst (final String s,final char sub,final char with) { int index = s.indexOf (sub);if (index == - 1) { return s;} char [ ] str = s.toCharArray ();str [ index ] = with;return new String (str);}

originalComment: Replaces the very last occurrence of a substring with supplied string.
codeComment: This method replaces the last occurrence of a substring `sub` in a string `s` with another string `with`. If `sub` is not found in `s`, it returns `s` unchanged.
codeFunctions: public static String replaceLast (final String s,final String sub,final String with) { int i = s.lastIndexOf (sub);if (i == - 1) { return s;} return s.substring (0,i) + with + s.substring (i + sub.length ());}

originalComment: Replaces the very last occurrence of a character in a string.
codeComment: This method replaces the last occurrence of a specified character in a string with another character. It first finds the last index of the specified character using `lastIndexOf`, then replaces the character at that index with the new character, and finally returns the modified string.
codeFunctions: public static String replaceLast (final String s,final char sub,final char with) { int index = s.lastIndexOf (sub);if (index == - 1) { return s;} char [ ] str = s.toCharArray ();str [ index ] = with;return new String (str);}

originalComment: Removes all substring occurrences from the string.
codeComment: This method removes all occurrences of a substring from a given string. It uses a `StringBuilder` to efficiently construct the resulting string without modifying the original string. The method first checks if the substring is empty, in which case it returns the original string. It then finds the first occurrence of the substring starting from the current index `c`. If the substring is not found, it returns the original string. Otherwise, it appends the part of the string before the found substring to the `StringBuilder`, updates the index `c` to the position after the found substring, and continues searching for the substring. Once all occurrences are removed, it appends the remaining part of the string to the `StringBuilder` and returns the resulting string.
codeFunctions: public static String remove (final String s,final String sub) { int c = 0;int sublen = sub.length ();if (sublen == 0) { return s;} int i = s.indexOf (sub,c);if (i == - 1) { return s;} StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (s.length ());do { sb.append (s,c,i);c = i + sublen;} while ((i = s.indexOf (sub,c)) != - 1);if (c < s.length ()) { sb.append (s,c,s.length ());} return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Removes a single character from string.
codeComment: This method removes all occurrences of a specified character from a given string. It iterates through the input string, copying characters to a new array if they are not equal to the specified character. If no changes are made, it returns the original string.
codeFunctions: public static String remove (final String string,final char ch) { int stringLen = string.length ();char [ ] result = new char [ stringLen ];int offset = 0;for (int i = 0;i < stringLen;i ++) { char c = string.charAt (i);if (c == ch) { continue;} result [ offset ] = c;offset ++;} if (offset == stringLen) { return string;// no changes } return new String (result,0,offset);}

originalComment: Determines if string array contains empty strings.
codeComment: The method `isAllEmpty` checks if all the provided strings are empty. It iterates over each string in the input array and returns `false` if any string is not empty. If all strings are empty, it returns `true`.
codeFunctions: public static boolean isAllEmpty (final String ... strings) { for (String string:strings) { if (!isEmpty (string)) { return false;} } return true;}

originalComment: Determines if string array contains just blank strings.
codeComment: This method checks if all the provided strings are blank. It iterates over each string in the input array and uses the `isBlank` method to determine if the string is blank. If any string is not blank, the method returns `false`. If all strings are blank, it returns `true`.
codeFunctions: public static boolean isAllBlank (final String ... strings) { for (String string:strings) { if (!isBlank (string)) { return false;} } return true;}

originalComment: Converts an array object to array of strings where every element of input array is converted to a string.If input is not an array the result will still be an array with one element.
codeComment: This method converts an object to a string array. If the input is null, it returns an empty string array. If the input is an array, it checks the type of the array's component type. If the component type is a primitive, it converts the array to a string array using the appropriate `ArraysUtil.toStringArray` method for that primitive type. If the component type is an object, it converts the array to a string array using the `ArraysUtil.toStringArray` method for objects. If the component type is not a primitive or an object, it throws an `IllegalArgumentException`.
codeFunctions: public static String [ ] toStringArray (final Object value) { if (value == null) { return new String [ 0 ];} Class <?> type = value.getClass ();if (!type.isArray ()) { return new String [ ] { value.toString () };} Class componentType = type.getComponentType ();if (componentType.isPrimitive ()) { if (componentType == int.class) { return ArraysUtil.toStringArray ((int [ ]) value);} else if (componentType == long.class) { return ArraysUtil.toStringArray ((long [ ]) value);} else if (componentType == double.class) { return ArraysUtil.toStringArray ((double [ ]) value);} else if (componentType == float.class) { return ArraysUtil.toStringArray ((float [ ]) value);} else if (componentType == boolean.class) { return ArraysUtil.toStringArray ((boolean [ ]) value);} else if (componentType == short.class) { return ArraysUtil.toStringArray ((short [ ]) value);} else if (componentType == byte.class) { return ArraysUtil.toStringArray ((byte [ ]) value);} else { throw new IllegalArgumentException ();} } else { return ArraysUtil.toStringArray ((Object [ ]) value);} }

originalComment: Internal method for changing the first character case.
codeComment: This method takes a boolean `capitalize` and a string `string` as input. It checks if the string is empty and returns it as is if true. Otherwise, it changes the case of the first character of the string based on the `capitalize` flag. If the case of the first character remains unchanged, it returns the original string. Otherwise, it converts the string to a character array, modifies the first character, and returns the modified string as a new string.
codeFunctions: private static String changeFirstCharacterCase (final boolean capitalize,final String string) { int strLen = string.length ();if (strLen == 0) { return string;} char ch = string.charAt (0);char modifiedCh;if (capitalize) { modifiedCh = Character.toUpperCase (ch);} else { modifiedCh = Character.toLowerCase (ch);} if (modifiedCh == ch) { // no change, return unchanged string return string;} char [ ] chars = string.toCharArray ();chars [ 0 ] = modifiedCh;return new String (chars);}

originalComment: Makes a title - cased string from given input.
codeComment: This method takes a string as input and capitalizes the first letter of each word, while leaving the rest of the letters in lowercase.
codeFunctions: public static String title (final String string) { char [ ] chars = string.toCharArray ();boolean wasWhitespace = true;for (int i = 0;i < chars.length;i ++) { char c = chars [ i ];if (CharUtil.isWhitespace (c)) { wasWhitespace = true;} else { if (wasWhitespace) { chars [ i ] = Character.toUpperCase (c);} else { chars [ i ] = Character.toLowerCase (c);} wasWhitespace = false;} } return new String (chars);}

originalComment: Compress multiple occurrences of given char into one appearance.
codeComment: This method compresses a string by removing consecutive occurrences of a specified character. It iterates through the input string, appending characters to a `StringBuilder` if they are not the specified character, or if they are the specified character but not consecutive. If no characters are removed, it returns the original string.
codeFunctions: public static String compressChars (final String s,final char c) { int len = s.length ();StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (len);boolean wasChar = false;for (int i = 0;i < len;i ++) { char c1 = s.charAt (i);if (c1 == c) { if (wasChar) { continue;} wasChar = true;} else { wasChar = false;} sb.append (c1);} if (sb.length () == len) { return s;} return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Tests if this string starts with the specified prefix with ignored case and with the specified prefix beginning a specified index.
codeComment: This method checks if the substring `subS` (case-insensitive) starts at the specified `startIndex` in the string `src`. It converts both the substring and the source string to lowercase for comparison. If the substring is longer than the remaining part of the source string starting from the given index, it returns false. Otherwise, it iterates through the characters of both strings, comparing them case-insensitively. If all characters match, it returns true; otherwise, it returns false.
codeFunctions: public static boolean startsWithIgnoreCase (final String src,final String subS,final int startIndex) { String sub = subS.toLowerCase ();int sublen = sub.length ();if (startIndex + sublen > src.length ()) { return false;} int j = 0;int i = startIndex;while (j < sublen) { char source = Character.toLowerCase (src.charAt (i));if (sub.charAt (j) != source) { return false;} j ++;i ++;} return true;}

originalComment: Returns if string ends with provided character.
codeComment: The method `endsWithChar` checks if a given string `s` ends with a specified character `c`. It returns `true` if the string is not empty and the last character of the string matches the specified character, otherwise it returns `false`.
codeFunctions: public static boolean endsWithChar (final String s,final char c) { if (s.length () == 0) { return false;} return s.charAt (s.length () - 1) == c;}

originalComment: Count substring occurrences in a source string ignoring case.
codeComment: This method counts the number of occurrences of a substring in a given string, ignoring case differences. It uses a helper method `indexOfIgnoreCase` to find the position of the substring within the source string starting from a specified index. The method returns the total count of occurrences.
codeFunctions: public static int countIgnoreCase (final String source,final String sub) { int count = 0;int j = 0;int sublen = sub.length ();if (sublen == 0) { return 0;} while (true) { int i = indexOfIgnoreCase (source,sub,j);if (i == - 1) { break;} count ++;j = i + sublen;} return count;}

originalComment: Compares two string arrays.
codeComment: The method `equalsIgnoreCase` checks if two arrays of strings are equal, ignoring case differences. It returns `true` if all corresponding elements are equal when compared in a case-insensitive manner, and `false` otherwise.
codeFunctions: public static boolean equalsIgnoreCase (final String [ ] as,final String [ ] as1) { if (as.length != as1.length) { return false;} for (int i = 0;i < as.length;i ++) { if (!as [ i ].equalsIgnoreCase (as1 [ i ])) { return false;} } return true;}

originalComment: Returns first index of a whitespace character starting from specified index offset.
codeComment: This method searches for the first whitespace character within a specified range of a string. It iterates through the characters from the start index to the end index, checking if each character is a whitespace using the `CharUtil.isWhitespace` method. If a whitespace character is found, it returns the index of that character. If no whitespace is found within the specified range, it returns -1.
codeFunctions: public static int indexOfWhitespace (final String string,final int startindex,final int endindex) { for (int i = startindex;i < endindex;i ++) { if (CharUtil.isWhitespace (string.charAt (i))) { return i;} } return - 1;}

originalComment: Strips leading char if string starts with one.
codeComment: This method removes the leading character `c` from the input string `string` if it exists. If the string is empty or does not start with `c`, it returns the original string.
codeFunctions: public static String stripLeadingChar (final String string,final char c) { if (string.length () > 0) { if (string.charAt (0) == c) { return string.substring (1);} } return string;}

originalComment: Strips trailing char if string ends with one.
codeComment: This method removes the trailing character `c` from the input string `string` if it exists. If the string is empty or does not end with the character `c`, it returns the original string.
codeFunctions: public static String stripTrailingChar (final String string,final char c) { if (string.length () > 0) { if (string.charAt (string.length () - 1) == c) { return string.substring (0,string.length () - 1);} } return string;}

originalComment: Strips leading and trailing char from given string.
codeComment: This method removes the first and last occurrences of a specified character from a given string. If the string is empty or contains only one character, it returns the string as is. Otherwise, it iterates through the string to find the first and last occurrences of the specified character and returns the substring excluding these occurrences.
codeFunctions: public static String stripChar (final String string,final char c) { if (string.length () == 0) { return string;} if (string.length () == 1) { if (string.charAt (0) == c) { return StringPool.EMPTY;} return string;} int left = 0;int right = string.length ();if (string.charAt (left) == c) { left ++;} if (string.charAt (right - 1) == c) { right --;} return string.substring (left,right);}

originalComment: Strips everything up to the first appearance of given char.Character IS included in the returned string.
codeComment: The `stripToChar` method takes a string and a character as input. It finds the index of the first occurrence of the character in the string. If the character is not found, it returns the original string. If the character is found, it returns a substring of the original string starting from the index of the character.
codeFunctions: public static String stripToChar (final String string,final char c) { int ndx = string.indexOf (c);if (ndx == - 1) { return string;} return string.substring (ndx);}

originalComment: Strips everything from the first appearance of given char.Character IS NOT included in the returned string.
codeComment: The `stripFromChar` method takes a string and a character as input. It finds the index of the first occurrence of the character in the string. If the character is not found, it returns the original string. Otherwise, it returns a substring of the original string from the start up to (but not including) the index of the character.
codeFunctions: public static String stripFromChar (final String string,final char c) { int ndx = string.indexOf (c);if (ndx == - 1) { return string;} return string.substring (0,ndx);}

originalComment: Crops all elements of string array.
codeComment: This method takes a variable number of string arguments, iterates over each string, and applies the `crop` method to it. If the string is not null, it replaces the original string with the result of the `crop` method.
codeFunctions: public static void cropAll (final String ... strings) { for (int i = 0;i < strings.length;i ++) { String string = strings [ i ];if (string != null) { string = crop (strings [ i ]);} strings [ i ] = string;} }

originalComment: Trim whitespaces from the left.
codeComment: This method trims leading whitespace characters from the input string `src`. It iterates through the string, starting from the beginning, and counts the number of leading whitespace characters. If there are any leading whitespace characters, it returns a substring of `src` starting from the first non-whitespace character. If there are no leading whitespace characters, it returns the original string.
codeFunctions: public static String trimLeft (final String src) { int len = src.length ();int st = 0;while ((st < len) && (CharUtil.isWhitespace (src.charAt (st)))) { st ++;} return st > 0?src.substring (st):src;}

originalComment: Trim whitespaces from the right.
codeComment: This method trims any trailing whitespace characters from the input string `src`. It iterates from the end of the string towards the beginning, checking each character to see if it is a whitespace character. Once it finds a non-whitespace character, it returns the substring from the start of the string up to that character. If there is no non-whitespace character, it returns the entire string.
codeFunctions: public static String trimRight (final String src) { int len = src.length ();int count = len;while ((len > 0) && (CharUtil.isWhitespace (src.charAt (len - 1)))) { len --;} return (len < count)?src.substring (0,len):src;}

originalComment: Returns indexes of the first region without escaping character.
codeComment: This method searches for the indices of the left and right boundaries within a given string, starting from a specified offset. It returns an array containing the start and end indices of the region defined by these boundaries. If either boundary is not found, it returns null.
codeFunctions: public static int [ ] indexOfRegion (final String string,final String leftBoundary,final String rightBoundary,final int offset) { int ndx = offset;int [ ] res = new int [ 4 ];ndx = string.indexOf (leftBoundary,ndx);if (ndx == - 1) { return null;} res [ 0 ] = ndx;ndx += leftBoundary.length ();res [ 1 ] = ndx;ndx = string.indexOf (rightBoundary,ndx);if (ndx == - 1) { return null;} res [ 2 ] = ndx;res [ 3 ] = ndx + rightBoundary.length ();return res;}

originalComment: Joins an collection of objects into one string with separator.
codeComment: This method takes a collection and a separator character as input and returns a string that is the concatenation of the elements in the collection, separated by the specified separator. If the collection is null or empty, it returns an empty string. The method uses a StringBuilder to efficiently build the resulting string.
codeFunctions: public static String join (final Collection collection,final char separator) { if (collection == null) { return null;} if (collection.size () == 0) { return StringPool.EMPTY;} final StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (collection.size () * 16);final Iterator it = collection.iterator ();for (int i = 0;i < collection.size ();i ++) { if (i > 0) { sb.append (separator);} sb.append (it.next ());} return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Joins an array of objects into one string with separator.
codeComment: This method takes an array of objects and a separator string as input. It returns a single string that is the concatenation of the array elements, separated by the specified separator. If the array is null, it returns null. If the array is empty, it returns an empty string. If the array has only one element, it returns the string representation of that element. Otherwise, it uses a StringBuilder to efficiently concatenate the elements of the array, appending the separator between each element.
codeFunctions: public static String join (final Object [ ] array,final String separator) { if (array == null) { return null;} if (array.length == 0) { return StringPool.EMPTY;} if (array.length == 1) { return String.valueOf (array [ 0 ]);} final StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (array.length * 16);for (int i = 0;i < array.length;i ++) { if (i > 0) { sb.append (separator);} sb.append (array [ i ]);} return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Converts string charset.If charset names are the same the same string is returned.
codeComment: This method converts the character encoding of a given string from one character set to another. If the source and new character sets are the same, it returns the original string. Otherwise, it converts the string's bytes from the source character set to the new character set using `StringUtil.getBytes` and `StringUtil.newString`.
codeFunctions: public static String convertCharset (final String source,final String srcCharsetName,final String newCharsetName) { if (srcCharsetName.equals (newCharsetName)) { return source;} return StringUtil.newString (StringUtil.getBytes (source,srcCharsetName),newCharsetName);}

originalComment: Safely compares provided char with char on given location.
codeComment: The method `isCharAtEqual` checks if the character at a specified index in a given string is equal to a specified character. It returns `true` if the character at the index matches the specified character, and `false` otherwise. The method first checks if the index is within the valid range of the string's length. If the index is out of bounds, it returns `false`. Otherwise, it compares the character at the specified index with the specified character and returns the result of the comparison.
codeFunctions: public static boolean isCharAtEqual (final String string,final int index,final char charToCompare) { if ((index < 0) || (index >= string.length ())) { return false;} return string.charAt (index) == charToCompare;}

originalComment: Surrounds the string with provided prefix and suffix if such missing from string.
codeComment: This method takes a string and surrounds it with a prefix and suffix if they are not already present. It first checks if the string starts with the prefix and adds it if it doesn't. Then, it checks if the string ends with the suffix and adds it if it doesn't. Finally, it returns the modified string.
codeFunctions: public static String surround (String string,final String prefix,final String suffix) { if (!string.startsWith (prefix)) { string = prefix + string;} if (!string.endsWith (suffix)) { string += suffix;} return string;}

originalComment: Inserts prefix if doesn t exist.
codeComment: This method takes a string and a prefix as input. If the string does not start with the given prefix, it prepends the prefix to the string and returns the modified string.
codeFunctions: public static String prefix (String string,final String prefix) { if (!string.startsWith (prefix)) { string = prefix + string;} return string;}

originalComment: Appends suffix if doesn t exist.
codeComment: This method appends a specified suffix to a given string if the string does not already end with that suffix.
codeFunctions: public static String suffix (String string,final String suffix) { if (!string.endsWith (suffix)) { string += suffix;} return string;}

originalComment: Cuts the string from beginning to the first index of provided substring.
codeComment: This method takes a string and a substring as input. It finds the index of the substring within the string using the `indexOf` method. If the substring is found, it removes the substring from the original string up to and including the found index. The modified string is then returned. If the substring is not found, the original string is returned unchanged.
codeFunctions: public static String cutToIndexOf (String string,final String substring) { int i = string.indexOf (substring);if (i != - 1) { string = string.substring (0,i);} return string;}

originalComment: Cuts the string from the first index of provided substring to the end.
codeComment: This method takes a string and a substring as input. It finds the index of the substring within the string using the `indexOf` method. If the substring is found, it returns the substring starting from the found index. If the substring is not found, it returns the original string.
codeFunctions: public static String cutFromIndexOf (String string,final String substring) { int i = string.indexOf (substring);if (i != - 1) { string = string.substring (i);} return string;}

originalComment: Cuts prefix if exists.
codeComment: This method takes a string and a prefix as input. If the string starts with the given prefix, it removes the prefix from the string and returns the modified string. Otherwise, it returns the original string.
codeFunctions: public static String cutPrefix (String string,final String prefix) { if (string.startsWith (prefix)) { string = string.substring (prefix.length ());} return string;}

originalComment: Cuts sufix if exists.
codeComment: This method takes a string and a suffix as input. It checks if the string ends with the given suffix. If it does, it removes the suffix from the string and returns the modified string. If the string does not end with the suffix, it returns the original string.
codeFunctions: public static String cutSuffix (String string,final String suffix) { if (string.endsWith (suffix)) { string = string.substring (0,string.length () - suffix.length ());} return string;}

originalComment: Removes surrounding prefix and suffixes.
codeComment: This method takes a string and removes any leading or trailing occurrences of a specified prefix and suffix. It returns the modified string or an empty string if the suffix is longer than the prefix or if the string does not contain either prefix or suffix.
codeFunctions: public static String cutSurrounding (final String string,final String prefix,final String suffix) { int start = 0;int end = string.length ();if (string.startsWith (prefix)) { start = prefix.length ();} if (string.endsWith (suffix)) { end -= suffix.length ();} if (end <= start) { return StringPool.EMPTY;} return string.substring (start,end);}

originalComment: Inserts a string on provided offset.
codeComment: This method inserts a specified string (`insert`) into another string (`src`) at a given offset. If the offset is less than 0, it is set to 0. If the offset is greater than the length of `src`, it is set to the length of `src`. The method then creates a `StringBuilder` from `src`, inserts the `insert` string at the specified offset, and returns the resulting string.
codeFunctions: public static String insert (final String src,final String insert,int offset) { if (offset < 0) { offset = 0;} if (offset > src.length ()) { offset = src.length ();} StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (src);sb.insert (offset,insert);return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Creates a new string that contains the provided string a number of times.
codeComment: This method takes a string `source` and an integer `count`, and returns a new string that is the result of repeating `source` `count` times. It uses a `StringBand` object to efficiently build the result string.
codeFunctions: public static String repeat (final String source,int count) { StringBand result = new StringBand (count);while (count > 0) { result.append (source);count --;} return result.toString ();}

originalComment: Reverse a string.
codeComment: Reverses the input string by iterating over it from the end to the beginning and appending each character to a `StringBuilder`.
codeFunctions: public static String reverse (final String s) { StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder (s.length ());for (int i = s.length () - 1;i >= 0;i --) { result.append (s.charAt (i));} return result.toString ();}

originalComment: Returns max common prefix of two strings.
codeComment: The method `maxCommonPrefix` takes two strings as input and returns the longest common prefix between them. It calculates the minimum length of the two strings and iterates through the characters of both strings up to that length. If the characters at the current position are not the same, it breaks the loop. Otherwise, it appends the character to a `StringBuilder`. Finally, it returns the common prefix as a string.
codeFunctions: public static String maxCommonPrefix (final String one,final String two) { final int minLength = Math.min (one.length (),two.length ());final StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder (minLength);for (int pos = 0;pos < minLength;pos ++) { final char currentChar = one.charAt (pos);if (currentChar != two.charAt (pos)) { break;} sb.append (currentChar);} return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Finds common prefix for several strings.Returns an empty string if arguments do not have a common prefix.
codeComment: The method `findCommonPrefix` takes a variable number of string arguments and returns the longest common prefix among them. It uses a `StringBuilder` to construct the prefix and iterates through each character of the strings, comparing them at the current index. If a mismatch is found or a string ends before the current index, the loop breaks. The method returns an empty string if no common prefix is found.
codeFunctions: public static String findCommonPrefix (final String ... strings) { StringBuilder prefix = new StringBuilder ();int index = 0;char c = 0;loop:while (true) { for (int i = 0;i < strings.length;i ++) { String s = strings [ i ];if (index == s.length ()) { break loop;} if (i == 0) { c = s.charAt (index);} else { if (s.charAt (index) != c) { break loop;} } } index ++;prefix.append (c);} return prefix.length () == 0?StringPool.EMPTY:prefix.toString ();}

originalComment: Shorten string to given length.
codeComment: This method takes a string `s`, a `length` parameter, and a `suffix` string. It first reduces the `length` by the length of the `suffix`. If the length of `s` is greater than the adjusted `length`, it finds the last whitespace character in the first `length` characters of `s` and truncates `s` at that point. The truncated string is then concatenated with the `suffix` and returned.
codeFunctions: public static String shorten (String s,int length,final String suffix) { length -= suffix.length ();if (s.length () > length) { for (int j = length;j >= 0;j --) { if (CharUtil.isWhitespace (s.charAt (j))) { length = j;break;} } String temp = s.substring (0,length);s = temp.concat (suffix);} return s;}

originalComment: Converts all of the characters in the string to upper case based on the locale.
codeComment: This method converts a given string to uppercase, handling non-ASCII characters by using the default locale. It iterates over each character in the string, checking if it's a non-ASCII character. If so, it falls back to using the default locale to convert the entire string to uppercase. If the character is a space, it converts it to lowercase by subtracting 32 from its ASCII value. If the string contains only ASCII characters, it returns the string in uppercase without any modifications.
codeFunctions: public static String toUpperCase (final String s,Locale locale) { if (s == null) { return null;} StringBuilder sb = null;for (int i = 0;i < s.length ();i ++) { char c = s.charAt (i);if (c > 127) { // found non-ascii char, fallback to the slow unicode detection if (locale == null) { locale = Locale.getDefault ();} return s.toUpperCase (locale);} if ((c >= ' ') && (c <= ' ')) { if (sb == null) { sb = new StringBuilder (s);} sb.setCharAt (i,(char) (c - 32));} } if (sb == null) { return s;} return sb.toString ();}

originalComment: Removes starting and ending single or double quotes.
codeComment: The method `removeQuotes` takes a string as input and checks if it starts and ends with a space. If it does, it removes the first and last characters of the string. If not, it returns the original string.
codeFunctions: public static String removeQuotes (final String string) { if ((startsWithChar (string,' ') && endsWithChar (string,' ')) || (startsWithChar (string,' ') && endsWithChar (string,' ')) || (startsWithChar (string,' ') && endsWithChar (string,' '))) { return substring (string,1,- 1);} return string;}

originalComment: Converts bytes to hex string.
codeComment: This method converts a byte array into a hexadecimal string. It iterates over each byte in the input array, converts it to a two-character hexadecimal string using the `CharUtil.int2hex` method, and appends it to a character array. Finally, it returns the character array as a string.
codeFunctions: public static String toHexString (final byte [ ] bytes) { char [ ] chars = new char [ bytes.length * 2 ];int i = 0;for (byte b:bytes) { chars [ i ++ ] = CharUtil.int2hex ((b & 0xF0) >> 4);chars [ i ++ ] = CharUtil.int2hex (b & 0x0F);} return new String (chars);}

originalComment: Returns String bytes using Jodds default encoding.
codeComment: This method converts a given string into a byte array using the encoding specified by `JoddCore.encoding`. If the specified encoding is not supported, it throws a `RuntimeException`.
codeFunctions: public static byte [ ] getBytes (final String string) { try { return string.getBytes (JoddCore.encoding);} catch (UnsupportedEncodingException e) { throw new RuntimeException (e);} }

originalComment: Detects quote character or return 0.
codeComment: The method `detectQuoteChar` checks if the input string `str` has a matching opening and closing quote character. It returns the quote character if found, otherwise returns 0.
codeFunctions: public static char detectQuoteChar (final String str) { if (str.length () < 2) { return 0;} final char c = str.charAt (0);if (c != str.charAt (str.length () - 1)) { return 0;} if (c == ' ' || c == ' ' || c == ' ') { return c;} return 0;}

originalComment: Visits a primitive value of the annotation.

codeFunctions: public void visit (final String name,final Object value) { if (av != null) { av.visit (name,value);} }

originalComment: Visits an enumeration value of the annotation.
codeComment: This method checks if an `AttributeVisitor` (`av`) is not null and, if so, calls its `visitEnum` method with the provided parameters: `name`, `descriptor`, and `value`.
codeFunctions: public void visitEnum (final String name,final String descriptor,final String value) { if (av != null) { av.visitEnum (name,descriptor,value);} }

originalComment: Visits a nested annotation value of the annotation.
codeComment: This method checks if an `AnnotationVisitor` (`av`) is not null. If it is not null, it calls the `visitAnnotation` method of the `av` object with the provided `name` and `descriptor` parameters. If `av` is null, it returns null.
codeFunctions: public AnnotationVisitor visitAnnotation (final String name,final String descriptor) { if (av != null) { return av.visitAnnotation (name,descriptor);} return null;}

originalComment: Registers just type and entity names.Enough for most usages.
codeComment: This method registers a new entity type with a database entity descriptor. It first creates a new descriptor for the given type, then checks if the type is already registered in the `descriptorsMap`. If it is, it checks if the new descriptor is the same as the existing one. If not, it throws a `DbOomException`. It also checks if the entity name is already mapped to another entity in the `entityNamesMap`. If it is, it throws a `DbOomException`. If the type and name are unique, it adds the descriptor to both maps and returns it.
codeFunctions: public < E > DbEntityDescriptor < E > registerType (final Class < E > type) { DbEntityDescriptor < E > ded = createDbEntityDescriptor (type);DbEntityDescriptor < E > existing = descriptorsMap.put (type,ded);if (log.isDebugEnabled ()) { log.debug ("Register " + type.getName () + " as " + ded.getTableName ());} if (existing != null) { if (ded.getType () == type) { return ded;} throw new DbOomException ("Type already registered: " + existing.getType ());} existing = entityNamesMap.put (ded.getEntityName (),ded);if (existing != null) { throw new DbOomException ("Name '" + ded.getEntityName () + "' already mapped to an entity: " + existing.getType ());} return ded;}

originalComment: Registers entity.Existing entity will be removed if exist so no exception will be thrown.

originalComment: Removes entity and returns removed descriptor.

codeFunctions: public < E > DbEntityDescriptor < E > removeEntity (final Class < E > type) { DbEntityDescriptor < E > ded = descriptorsMap.remove (type);if (ded == null) { ded = createDbEntityDescriptor (type);} entityNamesMap.remove (ded.getEntityName ());tableNamesMap.remove (ded.getTableName ());return ded;}

originalComment: Lookups for annotated properties.Caches all annotated properties on the first action class scan.
codeComment: This method retrieves annotated properties for a given class. It first checks if the properties are already cached. If not, it uses `ClassIntrospector` to get all property descriptors for the class. It then iterates over these descriptors, checking for annotations on fields, write methods, or read methods. If an annotation is found, the property descriptor is added to a list. Finally, the list is converted to an array and cached for future use. If no annotated properties are found, an empty array is returned.
codeFunctions: protected PropertyDescriptor [ ] lookupAnnotatedProperties (final Class type) { PropertyDescriptor [ ] properties = annotatedProperties.get (type);if (properties != null) { return properties;} ClassDescriptor cd = ClassIntrospector.get ().lookup (type);PropertyDescriptor [ ] allProperties = cd.getAllPropertyDescriptors ();List < PropertyDescriptor > list = new ArrayList <> ();for (PropertyDescriptor propertyDescriptor:allProperties) { Annotation ann = null;if (propertyDescriptor.getFieldDescriptor () != null) { ann = propertyDescriptor.getFieldDescriptor ().getField ().getAnnotation (annotations);} if (ann == null && propertyDescriptor.getWriteMethodDescriptor () != null) { ann = propertyDescriptor.getWriteMethodDescriptor ().getMethod ().getAnnotation (annotations);} if (ann == null && propertyDescriptor.getReadMethodDescriptor () != null) { ann = propertyDescriptor.getReadMethodDescriptor ().getMethod ().getAnnotation (annotations);} if (ann != null) { list.add (propertyDescriptor);} } if (list.isEmpty ()) { properties = EMPTY;} else { properties = list.toArray (new PropertyDescriptor [ 0 ]);} annotatedProperties.put (type,properties);return properties;}

originalComment: Detects database and configure DbOom engine.

originalComment: Closes this output stream causing any buffered data to be flushed and any further output data to throw an IOException.
codeComment: Closes the stream, flushing any buffered data to the underlying gzip stream if it exists, or writing any remaining buffered data to the output stream if it does not. Sets the closed flag to true.
codeFunctions: @ Override public void close () throws IOException { if (closed) { return;} if (gzipstream != null) { flushToGZip ();gzipstream.close ();gzipstream = null;} else { if (bufferCount > 0) { output.write (buffer,0,bufferCount);bufferCount = 0;} } output.close ();closed = true;}

originalComment: Writes the specified byte to our output stream.

codeFunctions: @ Override public void write (final int b) throws IOException { if (closed) { throw new IOException ("Cannot write to a closed output stream");} if (bufferCount >= buffer.length) { flushToGZip ();} buffer [ bufferCount ++ ] = (byte) b;}

originalComment: Filters requests to remove URL - based session identifiers.

codeFunctions: @ Override public void doFilter (final ServletRequest request,final ServletResponse response,final FilterChain chain) throws IOException,ServletException { HttpServletRequest httpRequest = (HttpServletRequest) request;HttpServletResponse httpResponse = (HttpServletResponse) response;if (isRequestedSessionIdFromURL (httpRequest)) { HttpSession session = httpRequest.getSession (false);if (session != null) { session.invalidate ();// clear session if session id in URL } } // wrap response to remove URL encoding HttpServletResponseWrapper wrappedResponse = new HttpServletResponseWrapper (httpResponse) { @ Override public String encodeRedirectUrl (final String url) { return url;} @ Override public String encodeRedirectURL (final String url) { return url;} @ Override public String encodeUrl (final String url) { return url;} @ Override public String encodeURL (final String url) { return url;} };chain.doFilter (request,wrappedResponse);}

originalComment: Saves attachment to a file.
codeComment: This method writes the contents of a data source to a specified file. It uses an input stream to read from the data source and an output stream to write to the file. If an I/O exception occurs during the process, it throws a `MailException`. Finally, it closes the input stream.
codeFunctions: public void writeToFile (final File destination) { InputStream input = null;final OutputStream output;try { input = getDataSource ().getInputStream ();output = new FileOutputStream (destination);StreamUtil.copy (input,output);} catch (final IOException ioex) { throw new MailException (ioex);} finally { StreamUtil.close (input);} }

originalComment: Appends argument to the existing description.

originalComment: Cleans unnecessary whitespaces.

codeFunctions: @ Override public void text (final CharSequence text) { if (!strip) { super.text (text);return;} int textLength = text.length ();char [ ] dest = new char [ textLength ];int ndx = 0;boolean regularChar = true;for (int i = 0;i < textLength;i ++) { char c = text.charAt (i);if (CharUtil.isWhitespace (c)) { if (regularChar) { regularChar = false;c = ' ';} else { continue;} } else { regularChar = true;} dest [ ndx ] = c;ndx ++;} if (regularChar || (ndx != 1)) { super.text (CharBuffer.wrap (dest,0,ndx));strippedCharsCount += textLength - ndx;} else { strippedCharsCount += textLength;} }

originalComment: Registers a converter for specified type.User must register converter for all super - classes as well.

originalComment: Selects nodes using CSS3 selector query.
codeComment: The method `select` takes a string `query` as input, parses it using the `CSSelly.parse` method, and then calls itself with the parsed selectors collection.
codeFunctions: public List < Node > select (final String query) { Collection < List < CssSelector >> selectorsCollection = CSSelly.parse (query);return select (selectorsCollection);}

originalComment: Selected nodes using pre - parsed CSS selectors.Take in consideration collection type for results grouping order.
codeComment: This method takes a collection of lists of CSS selectors and returns a list of nodes that match any of the selectors in the collection. It iterates over each list of selectors, processes them, and adds the matching nodes to the results list.
codeFunctions: public List < Node > select (final Collection < List < CssSelector > > selectorsCollection) { List < Node > results = new ArrayList <> ();for (List < CssSelector > selectors:selectorsCollection) { processSelectors (results,selectors);} return results;}

originalComment: Process selectors and keep adding results.
codeComment: This method processes a list of CSS selectors and adds the selected nodes to a results list. It first selects nodes from the root node using the provided selectors and then adds any nodes that are not already in the results list to it.
codeFunctions: protected void processSelectors (final List < Node > results,final List < CssSelector > selectors) { List < Node > selectedNodes = select (rootNode,selectors);for (Node selectedNode:selectedNodes) { if (!results.contains (selectedNode)) { results.add (selectedNode);} } }

originalComment: Selects nodes using CSS3 selector query and returns the very first one.
codeComment: This method selects the first node from the result of a query. If no nodes are selected, it returns null.
codeFunctions: public Node selectFirst (final String query) { List < Node > selectedNodes = select (query);if (selectedNodes.isEmpty ()) { return null;} return selectedNodes.get (0);}

originalComment: Walks over the child notes maintaining the tree order and not using recursion.
codeComment: This method iteratively processes a list of nodes, selecting nodes that match a given CSS selector and adding them to a result list. It then adds the children of each processed node to the front of the list to ensure they are processed in walking order.
codeFunctions: protected void walkDescendantsIteratively (final LinkedList < Node > nodes,final CssSelector cssSelector,final List < Node > result) { while (!nodes.isEmpty ()) { Node node = nodes.removeFirst ();selectAndAdd (node,cssSelector,result);// append children in walking order to be processed right after this node int childCount = node.getChildNodesCount ();for (int i = childCount - 1;i >= 0;i --) { nodes.addFirst (node.getChild (i));} } }

originalComment: Finds nodes in the tree that matches single selector.
codeComment: This method `walk` is designed to traverse a tree structure (represented by a `Node` object) based on a CSS selector. It uses a recursive approach to find nodes that match the given CSS selector. The method handles different types of combinators (DESCENDANT, CHILD, ADJACENT_SIBLING, and GENERAL_SIBLING) to determine how to traverse the tree. It uses a `LinkedList` to store child nodes and iteratively processes them to find matching nodes.
codeFunctions: protected void walk (final Node rootNode,final CssSelector cssSelector,final List < Node > result) { // previous combinator determines the behavior CssSelector previousCssSelector = cssSelector.getPrevCssSelector ();Combinator combinator = previousCssSelector != null?previousCssSelector.getCombinator ():Combinator.DESCENDANT;switch (combinator) { case DESCENDANT:LinkedList < Node > nodes = new LinkedList <> ();int childCount = rootNode.getChildNodesCount ();for (int i = 0;i < childCount;i ++) { nodes.add (rootNode.getChild (i));// recursive //					selectAndAdd(node, cssSelector, result); //					walk(node, cssSelector, result); } walkDescendantsIteratively (nodes,cssSelector,result);break;case CHILD:childCount = rootNode.getChildNodesCount ();for (int i = 0;i < childCount;i ++) { Node node = rootNode.getChild (i);selectAndAdd (node,cssSelector,result);} break;case ADJACENT_SIBLING:Node node = rootNode.getNextSiblingElement ();if (node != null) { selectAndAdd (node,cssSelector,result);} break;case GENERAL_SIBLING:node = rootNode;while (true) { node = node.getNextSiblingElement ();if (node == null) { break;} selectAndAdd (node,cssSelector,result);} break;} }

originalComment: Selects single node for single selector and appends it to the results.
codeComment: This method selects a node based on a CSS selector and adds it to a list if it is not a duplicate. It first checks if the node is an element, then checks if the CSS selector matches the node. If the node is not a duplicate, it is added to the result list.
codeFunctions: protected void selectAndAdd (final Node node,final CssSelector cssSelector,final List < Node > result) { // ignore all nodes that are not elements if (node.getNodeType () != Node.NodeType.ELEMENT) { return;} boolean matched = cssSelector.accept (node);if (matched) { // check for duplicates if (result.contains (node)) { return;} // no duplicate found, add it to the results result.add (node);} }

originalComment: Filter nodes.
codeComment: The method `filter` takes a list of `Node` objects, a `Node` object, a `CssSelector` object, and an integer index as parameters. It returns a boolean value indicating whether the `CssSelector` accepts the `Node` at the given index in the list.
codeFunctions: protected boolean filter (final List < Node > currentResults,final Node node,final CssSelector cssSelector,final int index) { return cssSelector.accept (currentResults,node,index);}

originalComment: Unpacks the compressed character translation table.
codeComment: This method unpacks a packed character map into an array of characters. It iterates over the packed string, reading the count and value for each character, and then writes the value to the unpacked array the specified number of times.
codeFunctions: private static char [ ] zzUnpackCMap (final String packed) { char [ ] map = new char [ 0x110000 ];int i = 0;/* index in packed string  */ int j = 0;/* index in unpacked array */ while (i < 128) { int count = packed.charAt (i ++);char value = packed.charAt (i ++);do map [ j ++ ] = value;while (-- count > 0);} return map;}

originalComment: Refills the input buffer.
codeComment: The method `zzRefill` checks if the `zzBuffer` is null. If it is, it assigns the `zzChars` array to `zzBuffer` and updates `zzEndRead` by adding the length of `zzChars`. The method returns `false` in this case. If `zzBuffer` is not null, it returns `true`.
codeFunctions: private boolean zzRefill () { if (zzBuffer == null) { zzBuffer = zzChars;zzEndRead += zzChars.length;return false;} return true;}

originalComment: Pages given page.
codeComment: This method constructs a paginated query for a given SQL statement, parameters, and sorting criteria. It calculates the offset for the query based on the page number and page size, builds the SQL for pagination and counting, executes the query, and returns a `PageData` object containing the page number, total count, page size, and list of results.
codeFunctions: protected < T > PageData < T > page (String sql,final Map params,final int page,final int pageSize,final String sortColumnName,final boolean ascending,final Class [ ] target) { if (sortColumnName != null) { sql = buildOrderSql (sql,sortColumnName,ascending);} int from = (page - 1) * pageSize;String pageSql = buildPageSql (sql,from,pageSize);DbSqlBuilder dbsql = sql (pageSql);DbOomQuery query = query (dbsql);query.setMaxRows (pageSize);query.setFetchSize (pageSize);query.setMap (params);List < T > list = query.list (pageSize,target);query.close ();String countSql = buildCountSql (sql);dbsql = sql (countSql);query = query (dbsql);query.setMap (params);long count = query.executeCount ();query.close ();return new PageData <> (page,(int) count,pageSize,list);}

originalComment: Removes the first select from the sql query.
codeComment: This method removes the "select" keyword from the beginning of a SQL query string. It first finds the index of the "select" keyword using `StringUtil.indexOfIgnoreCase`, and if found, it removes the substring starting from the index after "select" (which is 6 characters long).
codeFunctions: protected String removeSelect (String sql) { int ndx = StringUtil.indexOfIgnoreCase (sql,"select");if (ndx != - 1) { sql = sql.substring (ndx + 6);// select.length() } return sql;}

originalComment: Removes the first part of the sql up to the relevant from.Tries to detect sub - queries in the select part.
codeComment: This method removes the "from" clause from a SQL query if there are more "select" clauses to the left of it. It counts the number of "select" clauses to the left of the "from" clause and removes the "from" clause if the count is greater than or equal to the number of "select" clauses.
codeFunctions: protected String removeToFrom (String sql) { int from = 0;int fromCount = 1;int selectCount = 0;int lastNdx = 0;while (true) { int ndx = StringUtil.indexOfIgnoreCase (sql,"from",from);if (ndx == - 1) { break;} // count selects in left part String left = sql.substring (lastNdx,ndx);selectCount += StringUtil.countIgnoreCase (left,"select");if (fromCount >= selectCount) { sql = sql.substring (ndx);break;} // find next 'from' lastNdx = ndx;from = ndx + 4;fromCount ++;} return sql;}

originalComment: Removes everything from last order by.
codeComment: This method removes the last occurrence of the "order by" clause from a given SQL string. It first finds the index of "order by" using `StringUtil.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase`, then checks if this index is greater than the index of the last space in the string. If so, it removes the substring from the start of the string up to the "order by" clause.
codeFunctions: protected String removeLastOrderBy (String sql) { int ndx = StringUtil.lastIndexOfIgnoreCase (sql,"order by");if (ndx != - 1) { int ndx2 = sql.lastIndexOf (sql,' ');if (ndx > ndx2) { sql = sql.substring (0,ndx);} } return sql;}

originalComment: Decodes HTML text.Assumes that all character references are properly closed with semi - colon.
codeComment: This method decodes HTML entities in a given string. It iterates through the string, looking for HTML entities (sequences of characters that represent special characters). If it finds an entity, it replaces it with the corresponding character. If it finds a token (a sequence of characters that is not an entity), it replaces it with the corresponding character from a predefined map. If it finds a decimal or hexadecimal number, it converts it to an integer and appends the corresponding character to the result. If it finds a space, it appends the space to the result.
codeFunctions: public static String decode (final String html) { int ndx = html.indexOf (' ');if (ndx == - 1) { return html;} StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder (html.length ());int lastIndex = 0;int len = html.length ();mainloop:while (ndx != - 1) { result.append (html.substring (lastIndex,ndx));lastIndex = ndx;while (html.charAt (lastIndex) != ' ') { lastIndex ++;if (lastIndex == len) { lastIndex = ndx;break mainloop;} } if (html.charAt (ndx + 1) == ' ') { // decimal/hex char c = html.charAt (ndx + 2);int radix;if ((c == ' ') || (c == ' ')) { radix = 16;ndx += 3;} else { radix = 10;ndx += 2;} String number = html.substring (ndx,lastIndex);int i = Integer.parseInt (number,radix);result.append ((char) i);lastIndex ++;} else { // token String encodeToken = html.substring (ndx + 1,lastIndex);char [ ] replacement = ENTITY_MAP.get (encodeToken);if (replacement == null) { result.append (' ');lastIndex = ndx + 1;} else { result.append (replacement);lastIndex ++;} } ndx = html.indexOf (' ',lastIndex);} result.append (html.substring (lastIndex));return result.toString ();}

originalComment: Detects the longest character reference name on given position in char array.
codeComment: This method `detectName` takes a character array `input` and an integer `ndx` as input. It uses a binary search to find the longest name in the `ENTITY_NAMES` array that matches the characters starting from `ndx` in the input array. The method returns the longest matching name as a string, or `null` if no matching name is found.
codeFunctions: public static String detectName (final char [ ] input,int ndx) { final Ptr ptr = new Ptr ();int firstIndex = 0;int lastIndex = ENTITY_NAMES.length - 1;int len = input.length;char [ ] lastName = null;final BinarySearchBase binarySearch = new BinarySearchBase () { @ Override protected int compare (final int index) { char [ ] name = ENTITY_NAMES [ index ];if (ptr.offset >= name.length) { return - 1;} return name [ ptr.offset ] - ptr.c;} };while (true) { ptr.c = input [ ndx ];if (!CharUtil.isAlphaOrDigit (ptr.c)) { return lastName != null?new String (lastName):null;} firstIndex = binarySearch.findFirst (firstIndex,lastIndex);if (firstIndex < 0) { return lastName != null?new String (lastName):null;} char [ ] element = ENTITY_NAMES [ firstIndex ];if (element.length == ptr.offset + 1) { // total match, remember position, continue for finding the longer name lastName = ENTITY_NAMES [ firstIndex ];} lastIndex = binarySearch.findLast (firstIndex,lastIndex);if (firstIndex == lastIndex) { // only one element found, check the rest for (int i = ptr.offset;i < element.length;i ++) { if (element [ i ] != input [ ndx ]) { return lastName != null?new String (lastName):null;} ndx ++;} return new String (element);} ptr.offset ++;ndx ++;if (ndx == len) { return lastName != null?new String (lastName):null;} } }

originalComment: Appends ORDER BY keyword.
codeComment: This method appends an "order by" clause to the input SQL string based on the provided column and ascending flag. If the ascending flag is false, it appends "desc" to the SQL string.
codeFunctions: @ Override protected String buildOrderSql (String sql,final String column,final boolean ascending) { sql += " order by " + column;if (!ascending) { sql += " desc";} return sql;}

originalComment: Builds page sql using LIMIT keyword after the SELECT.
codeComment: This method overrides the `buildPageSql` method in a superclass. It removes the `SELECT` keyword from the input SQL query, then constructs a new SQL query that includes a `LIMIT` clause to paginate the results. The `LIMIT` clause specifies the starting index (`from`) and the number of rows to return (`pageSize`).
codeFunctions: @ Override protected String buildPageSql (String sql,final int from,final int pageSize) { sql = removeSelect (sql);return "select LIMIT " + from + ' ' + pageSize + sql;}

originalComment: Resolves list of all columns and properties.
codeComment: This method resolves column and property descriptors for a given class, checks for duplicate column names, and extracts ID columns. It uses `ClassIntrospector` to get all property descriptors and `DbMetaUtil.resolveColumnDescriptors` to resolve column descriptors. It also checks for duplicate column names and throws an exception if found. If no column mappings are found, it throws an exception. Finally, it sorts the column descriptors and extracts ID columns if any.
codeFunctions: private void resolveColumnsAndProperties (final Class type) { PropertyDescriptor [ ] allProperties = ClassIntrospector.get ().lookup (type).getAllPropertyDescriptors ();List < DbEntityColumnDescriptor > decList = new ArrayList <> (allProperties.length);int idcount = 0;HashSet < String > names = new HashSet <> (allProperties.length);for (PropertyDescriptor propertyDescriptor:allProperties) { DbEntityColumnDescriptor dec = DbMetaUtil.resolveColumnDescriptors (this,propertyDescriptor,isAnnotated,columnNamingStrategy);if (dec != null) { if (!names.add (dec.getColumnName ())) { throw new DbOomException ("Duplicate column name: " + dec.getColumnName ());} decList.add (dec);if (dec.isId) { idcount ++;} } } if (decList.isEmpty ()) { throw new DbOomException ("No column mappings in entity: " + type);} columnDescriptors = decList.toArray (new DbEntityColumnDescriptor [ 0 ]);Arrays.sort (columnDescriptors);// extract ids from sorted list if (idcount > 0) { idColumnDescriptors = new DbEntityColumnDescriptor [ idcount ];idcount = 0;for (DbEntityColumnDescriptor dec:columnDescriptors) { if (dec.isId) { idColumnDescriptors [ idcount ++ ] = dec;} } } }

originalComment: Finds column descriptor by column name.Case is ignored.
codeComment: This method searches for a `DbEntityColumnDescriptor` by its column name. It first checks if the input column name is null, returning null if it is. It then initializes the column descriptors and iterates through them, comparing the input column name with each descriptor's column name using a case-insensitive comparison. If a match is found, it returns the corresponding descriptor; otherwise, it returns null.
codeFunctions: public DbEntityColumnDescriptor findByColumnName (final String columnName) { if (columnName == null) { return null;} init ();for (DbEntityColumnDescriptor columnDescriptor:columnDescriptors) { if (columnDescriptor.columnName.equalsIgnoreCase (columnName)) { return columnDescriptor;} } return null;}

originalComment: Finds column descriptor by property name.
codeComment: This method searches for a `DbEntityColumnDescriptor` by its property name. It first checks if the provided property name is null, returning null if it is. Then, it initializes the column descriptors. It iterates through the list of column descriptors, checking if the property name of each descriptor matches the provided property name. originalComment: Creates scoped proxy bean for given bean definition.
codeComment: This method creates a scoped proxy bean for a given bean definition in a PetiteContainer. It first checks if a proxy class for the bean type already exists in the proxyClasses map. If not, it creates a new proxy class using Proxetta, a proxy generation library. The proxy class is configured with the specified aspect and a suffix. ProxettaBeanDefinition pbd = (ProxettaBeanDefinition) refBeanDefinition;ProxyProxetta proxetta = Proxetta.proxyProxetta ().withAspects (ArraysUtil.insert (pbd.proxyAspects,aspect,0));proxetta.setClassNameSuffix ("$ScopedProxy");proxetta.setVariableClassName (true);ProxyProxettaFactory builder = proxetta.proxy ().setTarget (pbd.originalTarget);proxyClass = builder.define ();proxyClasses.put (beanType,proxyClass);} else { ProxyProxetta proxetta = Proxetta.proxyProxetta ().withAspect (aspect);proxetta.setClassNameSuffix ("$ScopedProxy");proxetta.setVariableClassName (true);ProxyProxettaFactory builder = proxetta.proxy ().setTarget (beanType);proxyClass = builder.define ();proxyClasses.put (beanType,proxyClass);} } Object proxy;try { proxy = ClassUtil.newInstance (proxyClass);Field field = proxyClass.getField ("$__petiteContainer$0");field.set (proxy,petiteContainer);field = proxyClass.getField ("$__name$0");field.set (proxy,refBeanDefinition.name);} catch (Exception ex) { throw new PetiteException (ex);} return proxy;}

originalComment: Returns the size of the field_info JVMS structure generated by this FieldWriter.Also adds the names of the attributes of this field in the constant pool.
codeComment: This method calculates the size of a field in a Java class file based on its access flags, name, descriptor, and attributes. It adds the size of the access flags, name index, descriptor index, and attributes count fields, which are each 8 bytes. If the field has a constant value, synthetic, signature, or deprecated attribute, it adds the corresponding size (8, 6, 8, or 6 bytes, respectively). It also adds the size of any runtime-visible or runtime-invisible annotations and type annotations. Finally, it returns the total size of the field.
codeFunctions: int computeFieldInfoSize () { // The access_flags, name_index, descriptor_index and attributes_count fields use 8 bytes. int size = 8;// For ease of reference, we use here the same attribute order as in Section 4.7 of the JVMS. if (constantValueIndex != 0) { // ConstantValue attributes always use 8 bytes. symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.CONSTANT_VALUE);size += 8;} // Before Java 1.5, synthetic fields are represented with a Synthetic attribute. if ((accessFlags & Opcodes.ACC_SYNTHETIC) != 0 && symbolTable.getMajorVersion () < Opcodes.V1_5) { // Synthetic attributes always use 6 bytes. symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.SYNTHETIC);size += 6;} if (signatureIndex != 0) { // Signature attributes always use 8 bytes. symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.SIGNATURE);size += 8;} // ACC_DEPRECATED is ASM specific, the ClassFile format uses a Deprecated attribute instead. if ((accessFlags & Opcodes.ACC_DEPRECATED) != 0) { // Deprecated attributes always use 6 bytes. symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.DEPRECATED);size += 6;} if (lastRuntimeVisibleAnnotation != null) { size += lastRuntimeVisibleAnnotation.computeAnnotationsSize (Constants.RUNTIME_VISIBLE_ANNOTATIONS);} if (lastRuntimeInvisibleAnnotation != null) { size += lastRuntimeInvisibleAnnotation.computeAnnotationsSize (Constants.RUNTIME_INVISIBLE_ANNOTATIONS);} if (lastRuntimeVisibleTypeAnnotation != null) { size += lastRuntimeVisibleTypeAnnotation.computeAnnotationsSize (Constants.RUNTIME_VISIBLE_TYPE_ANNOTATIONS);} if (lastRuntimeInvisibleTypeAnnotation != null) { size += lastRuntimeInvisibleTypeAnnotation.computeAnnotationsSize (Constants.RUNTIME_INVISIBLE_TYPE_ANNOTATIONS);} if (firstAttribute != null) { size += firstAttribute.computeAttributesSize (symbolTable);} return size;}

It then writes the access_flags, name_index, and descriptor_index fields to the ByteVector. It computes the attributes_count field by counting the number of attributes that are present in the field. It then writes the attributes to the ByteVector in the order specified in the JVMS.

// For ease of reference, we use here the same attribute order as in Section 4.7 of the JVMS. int attributesCount = 0;if (constantValueIndex != 0) { ++ attributesCount;} if ((accessFlags & Opcodes.ACC_SYNTHETIC) != 0 && useSyntheticAttribute) { ++ attributesCount;} if (signatureIndex != 0) { ++ attributesCount;} if ((accessFlags & Opcodes.ACC_DEPRECATED) != 0) { ++ attributesCount;} if (lastRuntimeVisibleAnnotation != null) { ++ attributesCount;} if (lastRuntimeInvisibleAnnotation != null) { ++ attributesCount;} if (lastRuntimeVisibleTypeAnnotation != null) { ++ attributesCount;} if (lastRuntimeInvisibleTypeAnnotation != null) { ++ attributesCount;} if (firstAttribute != null) { attributesCount += firstAttribute.getAttributeCount ();} output.putShort (attributesCount);// Put the field_info attributes. // For ease of reference, we use here the same attribute order as in Section 4.7 of the JVMS. if (constantValueIndex != 0) { output.putShort (symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.CONSTANT_VALUE)).putInt (2).putShort (constantValueIndex);} if ((accessFlags & Opcodes.ACC_SYNTHETIC) != 0 && useSyntheticAttribute) { output.putShort (symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.SYNTHETIC)).putInt (0);} if (signatureIndex != 0) { output.putShort (symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.SIGNATURE)).putInt (2).putShort (signatureIndex);} if ((accessFlags & Opcodes.ACC_DEPRECATED) != 0) { output.putShort (symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.DEPRECATED)).putInt (0);} if (lastRuntimeVisibleAnnotation != null) { lastRuntimeVisibleAnnotation.putAnnotations (symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.RUNTIME_VISIBLE_ANNOTATIONS),output);} if (lastRuntimeInvisibleAnnotation != null) { lastRuntimeVisibleTypeAnnotation.putAnnotations (symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.RUNTIME_VISIBLE_TYPE_ANNOTATIONS),output);} if (lastRuntimeInvisibleTypeAnnotation != null) { lastRuntimeInvisibleTypeAnnotation.putAnnotations (symbolTable.addConstantUtf8 (Constants.RUNTIME_INVISIBLE_TYPE_ANNOTATIONS),output);} if (firstAttribute != null) { firstAttribute.putAttributes originalComment: Writes decorated content.
codeComment: This method writes a decorated page by iterating over a list of `DecoraTag` objects. It copies content before each tag, writes the content of the tag, and then writes the content after the tag. If a tag has a default value, it writes that instead of the tag's content. The method handles cases where the tag's start index is less than or equal to the current index, and it writes the remaining content after the last tag.
codeFunctions: protected void writeDecoratedPage (final Writer out,final char [ ] decoratorContent,final char [ ] pageContent,final DecoraTag [ ] decoraTags) throws IOException { int ndx = 0;for (DecoraTag decoraTag:decoraTags) { // [1] just copy content before the Decora tag int decoratorLen = decoraTag.getStartIndex () - ndx;if (decoratorLen <= 0) { continue;} out.write (decoratorContent,ndx,decoratorLen);ndx = decoraTag.getEndIndex ();// [2] now write region at the place of Decora tag int regionLen = decoraTag.getRegionLength ();if (regionLen == 0) { if (decoraTag.hasDefaultValue ()) { out.write (decoratorContent,decoraTag.getDefaultValueStart (),decoraTag.getDefaultValueLength ());} } else { writeRegion (out,pageContent,decoraTag,decoraTags);} } // write remaining content out.write (decoratorContent,ndx,decoratorContent.length - ndx);}

originalComment: Writes region to output but extracts all inner regions.
codeComment: This method writes content from a page to a writer, excluding content within specific decora tags. It iterates over a list of decora tags, checking for regions and writing content accordingly.
codeFunctions: protected void writeRegion (final Writer out,final char [ ] pageContent,final DecoraTag decoraTag,final DecoraTag [ ] decoraTags) throws IOException { int regionStart = decoraTag.getRegionStart ();int regionLen = decoraTag.getRegionLength ();int regionEnd = regionStart + regionLen;for (DecoraTag innerDecoraTag:decoraTags) { if (decoraTag == innerDecoraTag) { continue;} if (decoraTag.isRegionUndefined ()) { continue;} if (innerDecoraTag.isInsideOtherTagRegion (decoraTag)) { // write everything from region start to the inner Decora tag out.write (pageContent,regionStart,innerDecoraTag.getRegionTagStart () - regionStart);regionStart = innerDecoraTag.getRegionTagEnd ();} } // write remaining content of the region out.write (pageContent,regionStart,regionEnd - regionStart);}

originalComment: Starts HTTP tunnel.Method ends when the tunnel is stopped.

originalComment: Applies rules on given flag.Flag is only changed if at least one rule matched.Otherwise the same value is returned.This way you can chain several rules and have the rule engine change the flag only when a rule is matched.
codeComment: The method `apply` takes three parameters: `value`, `blacklist`, and `flag`. It checks if the `rules` object is null. If it is, the method returns the current value of `flag`. If `blacklist` is true, it processes the excludes and includes rules for the `value` and updates `flag` accordingly. If `blacklist` is false, it processes the includes and excludes rules for the `value` and updates `flag` accordingly. Finally, it returns the updated `flag`.
codeFunctions: public boolean apply (final V value,final boolean blacklist,boolean flag) { if (rules == null) { return flag;} if (blacklist) { flag = processExcludes (value,flag);flag = processIncludes (value,flag);} else { flag = processIncludes (value,flag);flag = processExcludes (value,flag);} return flag;}

originalComment: Process includes rules.
codeComment: This method checks if a given value should be included based on a set of rules. It iterates through the rules and checks if the value matches any of the rules. If a match is found, it sets the `include` flag to true and breaks out of the loop. If no match is found, it returns the original `include` value.

   - It uses the `propsData.extract` method to extract properties from the `target` map based on the lookup profiles and wildcards.
   - It iterates over the entries in the `target` map, constructs new keys and values, and puts them into the `propsData` map using the `putBaseProperty` or `putProfileProperty` methods, depending on whether `profiles` is null or not.

2. **QUICK_APPEND Operation**:
   - If the `operator` is `Operator.QUICK_APPEND`, it checks if `keyProfiles` is null.
   - If `keyProfiles` is null, it puts the `key` and `value` into the `propsData` map using the `putBaseProperty` method with the `append` flag.

codeComment: This method `typedescToSignature` takes a type description string `desc` and a mutable integer `from` as input. It processes the string to convert it into a Java method signature. codeFunctions: public static String typedescToSignature (final String desc,final MutableInteger from) { int fromIndex = from.get ();from.value ++;// default usage for most cases switch (desc.charAt (fromIndex)) { case ' ':return "byte";case ' ':return "char";case ' ':return "double";case ' ':return "float";case ' ':return "int";case ' ':return "long";case ' ':return "short";case ' ':return "boolean";case ' ':return "void";case ' ':int index = desc.indexOf (' ',fromIndex);if (index < 0) { throw new IllegalArgumentException (INVALID_TYPE_DESCRIPTION + desc);} from.set (index + 1);String str = desc.substring (fromIndex + 1,index);return str.replace (' ',' ');case ' ':return desc.substring (from.value);case ' ':StringBuilder brackets = new StringBuilder ();int n = fromIndex;while (desc.charAt (n) == ' ') { // count opening brackets brackets.append ("[]");n ++;} from.value = n;String type = typedescToSignature (desc,from);// the rest of the string denotes a `<field_type>' return type + brackets;default:if (from.value == 0) { throw new IllegalArgumentException (INVALID_TYPE_DESCRIPTION + desc);} // generics! return desc.substring (from.value);} }

originalComment: Finds the basic blocks that belong to the subroutine starting with the basic block corresponding to this label and marks these blocks as belonging to this subroutine.This method follows the control flow graph to find all the blocks that are reachable from the current basic block WITHOUT following any jsr target.
codeComment: The method `markSubroutine` takes a `short` parameter `subroutineId` and performs a data flow algorithm to mark basic blocks belonging to the specified subroutine. It uses a linked list to manage the blocks to be processed. The algorithm iteratively removes blocks from the list, marks them as belonging to the specified subroutine, and adds their successors to the list. If a block is already marked, it skips adding its successors.

Label listOfBlocksToProcess = this;listOfBlocksToProcess.nextListElement = EMPTY_LIST;while (listOfBlocksToProcess != EMPTY_LIST) { // Remove a basic block from the list of blocks to process. originalComment: Finds the basic blocks that end a subroutine starting with the basic block corresponding to this label and for each one of them adds an outgoing edge to the basic block following the given subroutine call.In other words completes the control flow graph by adding the edges corresponding to the return from this subroutine when called from the given caller basic block.
codeComment: This method implements a data flow algorithm to process basic blocks belonging to a subroutine starting with a given label. It adds return edges to the successor of the subroutine caller if applicable and adds its successor basic blocks to the list of blocks to process. originalComment: Compare digits at certain position in two strings.The longest run of digits wins.That aside the greatest value wins.
codeComment: This method compares two strings for equal digits, considering leading spaces and zero counts. It returns an array indicating the difference in length, equal digits, or zero counts between the two strings.
